Introduce yourself by showing one task from an ordinary school day. Ask students for their own example before showing syntax. On the board, draw two columns for price and balance. Ask one student to be the loop and another to decide which label appears. Change only the budget, predict the screen, then save the file and observe Fast Refresh. A stale phone screen and a wrong arithmetic result call for different investigations.

Point at the two Card elements in the parent. They call the same component definition with different names. Predict the result of moving useState above the component and passing one counter into both cards. A parent holding one number would make both displays follow that number. To keep a shared total and individual counts, store a map keyed by office and derive the total from it.

Sketch two boxes across a narrow phone. If both have large fixed widths, the second can leave the screen. Flexbox chooses how children share the main axis. Try flex:1 on the wide-screen cards to distribute the available width. Set a descriptive accessibilityLabel only when the visible text does not already describe the control. Check the order a screen reader will visit the labels.

Trace a single keystroke. The native input reports the entire new string. The setter stores it, React renders again, and value puts the same string back into the control. If value is fixed to an empty string while the handler merely logs changes, the student can type but sees no lasting change. Ask the class to reproduce that defect on a copy, then restore the setter.

On the board, draw a stack with Home at the bottom. Push an office once, press Back, and erase only the top box. A tab switch instead selects a peer section. Show how two different office IDs reuse one route file. Refresh that detail screen directly: if it depends on a prior click's global object, there is nothing to restore. Loading by ID or showing a missing-record message makes the screen understandable.

Trace the Clinic row through an update. Its key survives filtering because it comes from the record. The toggle returns the original object for every unaffected row. This lets React identify what actually changed. A query field can stay local while the same underlying task records are edited by multiple screens. Ask when a reducer would make action rules easier to test than a collection of setters.

Write the three outcomes of GET on the board: connection failed, response arrived with a failing status, and success with an empty list. Ask students to choose different wording for each. Compare the phone's result with the server terminal. Seeing a 404 in the log proves that changing Wi-Fi is unlikely to fix that route. Receiving an HTML error page also explains why JSON parsing may fail.

Model the same record twice. In SQL, title and done are columns and id is the primary key. In MongoDB, the document contains those fields and an _id. Inspect the adapter on each server: both transform storage identity to a string in JSON. PATCH a missing ID and compare its 404 with a blank-title rejection. That distinction lets a client offer refresh for a deleted record and inline correction for invalid input.

Draw two boxes labeled phone and server. Put a saved draft in the phone box. Switch off networking and restore it. Draw a separate pending edit arrow to the server, with a client-generated operation ID. Discuss what should happen if the server accepted it but the acknowledgment was lost. A retry needs identity and a conflict policy before this design can be called reliable offline synchronization.

Have one student read a count of three while another posts a fourth record. The first student's cache stays at three until a refetch or deliberate cache update. Query keys identify different result sets, so a filtered list may require its own invalidation policy. Try stopping the API after reading the count. A visible old count can be useful if the app labels it stale and offers a recovery action.

Draw a table with actor, record owner and decision. Ana reading Ana is allowed. Ana reading Ben is forbidden. A missing or expired verified session is unauthenticated. Change the record ID while keeping the actor fixed. The server must perform the ownership check again. A mock session exercises the interface, while a real sign-in integration requires a verified credential, secure redirects and server-side controls.

Draw three possible results after Take photo: permission denied, picker cancelled, and an asset returned. Only the last branch should replace the preview. If a previous photo exists and the next capture is cancelled, decide whether keeping it is less surprising than clearing it. A student who declines camera access must still be able to finish a text-only report.

Separate four moments: request permission, register a schedule, deliver a notification, and tap it. Each has different evidence. A notification tap might arrive while a screen is closed, so route using validated notification data. Contrast a review reminder with a background sync job. The latter should tolerate delays, repeated runs and interrupted network access.

Ask the class what information is necessary for a meetup. A public place name and map link can be sufficient. Opening a share sheet gives the user control of the recipient. Foreground location can suggest nearby offices without storing a trail. Before adding background location, identify a requirement that actually needs continuous updates and describe how the user could stop them.

Run the cue twice and notice that Play rewinds before starting again. Without seeking, pressing Play after Pause would resume. Show how the label follows player status rather than guessing from the last button pressed. For performance, compare a small list and a list with many large image previews in the same release configuration. Record a measurement before deciding which change improved it.

Ask students to identify the boundary where a private provider key belongs. The mobile app calls a campus API. That API can enforce limits, remove personal data and choose a fallback before calling a provider. An API route or a cloud function still needs a deployed server runtime. Compare a provider outage with an empty but valid response and choose separate messages.

Make the validation rule a sentence, then choose the values just below, at and just above each boundary. Add 79, 80 and 81 character cases. An implementation that returns true for every nonblank input passes some examples but fails 81. For release rehearsal, list which change only touches JS and which introduces a native permission or library. Match the delivery method to the actual change.

For your project diagram, label the owner of each state value. The search field belongs to the screen, the stored task belongs to the backend, and the loading message describes an in-flight operation. Add one project-specific acceptance criterion such as reopening a finished errand. Have a classmate reproduce it using only your setup notes and sample data.

Use a three-column repair log: input, expected, observed. Start with three spaces, Rejected, Accepted. This gives a precise defect to reproduce after each edit. For an API problem, record the status code and an anonymized sample body. Finish by explaining why the repair belongs in the screen, server or both. This is rehearsal for the independent practical.

Start the five-minute demo from the submitted copy. Spend the first minute naming the user and problem, two minutes on the working path, one minute on failure recovery and one minute tracing your own change. If the app uses a database, show a reload from a second client. Tick the rehearsal checklist only after someone can explain what the evidence demonstrates.
